Maya: Hey team, customer (acct: acme-inc) tried to stream to /v1/rerank and got a 415. They said they were using SSE. Any quick pointers?
Alex: Streaming to rerank isn't supported - rerank expects a single JSON POST. Do you have their curl?
Maya: Pasting what they used:
```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
     -H 'Content-Type: text/event-stream' \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
     -d '{"queries":["q1"],"documents":["d1","d2"]}'
```
Priya: Yep, 415 makes total sense. They set Content-Type to text/event-stream which our rerank handler rejects. Rerank expects application/json.
Ryan: If they need streaming UX, recommend they either do client-side streaming and batch up into a single rerank call, or use a streaming-capable ranking endpoint (not /v1/rerank). We don't support chunked SSE on rerank.
Maya: They also reported odd scores (all 0.0) after switching to JSON. Could that be tokenization/truncation hitting limits?
Alex: Possible. If documents exceed token limits we currently truncate which can produce bad scores. Ask them to check server logs for request-id and response body. Also check they're sending non-empty docs.
Maya: Error body they saw originally:
```
{"error":"unsupported content type 'text/event-stream' for route /v1/rerank"}
```
Priya: Repro steps I used locally (works):
```
curl -X POST 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -d '{"queries":["Which doc is best?"],"documents":["Doc A text","Doc B text"]}'
```
Response: 200 + JSON with scores array.
Alex: Also tell them not to put keys in the querystring (we sometimes see 401s). And if they're hammering small streaming requests they might hit rate limits; suggest batching.
Maya: Customer also mentioned seeing a 413 once. I told them that large payloads will be rejected; split docs or compress.
Ryan: If they still have problems, collect: full curl, exact response body, request-id header, account id, and timestamp, then escalate to eng-runtime. We'll grep logs (request-id helps).

Maya: thanks — sending now.
